name: manual_15aa46
claim: When a stacked-PR-family branch's earlier commits have already landed upstream via a different merge (e.g. a sibling PR's squash-merge), git rebase origin/master auto-detects patch-content equivalence and drops the now-redundant commits, printing 'dropping <sha> ... -- patch contents already upstream'; treat that message as confirmation of successful recovery, not an error, and use rebase as the recovery mechanic instead of manual cherry-pick surgery.

decisions.notes: Confirmed recovering 3 stacked agentic-stack upstream PR branches after sibling PR #60 (recall-supersession-filter) had independently merged; rebase cleanly dropped the now-redundant commit and left only the genuinely new content from #61/#62 to resolve.

rationale: Confirmed recovering 3 stacked agentic-stack upstream PR branches after sibling PR #60 (recall-supersession-filter) had independently merged; rebase cleanly dropped the now-redundant commit and left only the genuinely new content from #61/#62 to resolve.
